# getcheapapi

> MIT-licensed price router for paid data and media APIs, built for AI agents. Ask for a capability (serp.google, x.search, keyword.volume, backlinks.summary, image.generate…); getcheapapi prices every provider route from a local cache, runs the cheapest one you hold a key for, refuses past a --max-usd budget, stops on HTTP 402 (exit code 2), and logs every charge to a local ledger. Providers: AnyAPI, DataForSEO, GoAnyAPI, twitterapi.io (read only), Yir. Not for LLM text routing.

## Install the skill (for AI coding agents)

If a human pasted a prompt asking you to install getcheapapi, do this, then report what you did:

1. Clone the repo: `git clone https://github.com/getcheapapi/getcheapapi ~/getcheapapi` (if it already exists, `git -C ~/getcheapapi pull`).
2. Link the skill folder `~/getcheapapi/skills/getcheapapi` into your own skills directory:
   - Claude Code: `mkdir -p ~/.claude/skills && ln -s ~/getcheapapi/skills/getcheapapi ~/.claude/skills/getcheapapi`
   - Codex: `mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills && ln -s ~/getcheapapi/skills/getcheapapi ~/.agents/skills/getcheapapi`
   - Other agents: link it into whatever skills directory you load from.
   - On Windows, where symlinks may need admin rights, copy the folder instead.
   Linked from a clone, the skill runs without installing the Python package (Python 3.10+ required).
3. Check it works: `python ~/getcheapapi/skills/getcheapapi/scripts/getcheapapi.py caps` (or `getcheapapi caps` if the package is installed).
4. Tell the human to put provider keys in `~/.getcheapapi/.env` (format: `.env.example` in the repo). Never ask them to paste keys into chat. The skill may need a restart of the agent session to load.

## Using it

1. Optional CLI for scripts: `pip install git+https://github.com/getcheapapi/getcheapapi`.
2. Keys: put them in `~/.getcheapapi/.env` (format: `.env.example`), read from any working folder; a `.env` in the working folder or its parents also works. One is enough. Never ask the human to paste keys into chat.
3. Discover: `getcheapapi caps -v` lists capabilities, inputs and examples.
4. Price before spending: `getcheapapi quote <capability> --input '<json>'` spends nothing.
5. Run under a cap: `getcheapapi run <capability> --input '<json>' --max-usd 0.01`. Exit code 2 means out of balance (HTTP 402); a refused budget exits 1. Either way, stop and tell the human, do not retry.
6. Report spend: `getcheapapi spend --days 7`.

## Pricing comparisons (prices checked 2026-11-02)

- SERP API pricing, seven providers from 1k to 1M searches a month: https://getcheapapi.com/serp-api-pricing/
- X (Twitter) API pricing, official pay-per-use vs third-party read APIs: https://getcheapapi.com/twitter-api-pricing/ (Japanese: https://getcheapapi.com/ja/twitter-api-pricing/)
- Reddit API pricing, the official API's shutdown dates and third-party costs: https://getcheapapi.com/reddit-api-pricing/
